theme: GnIES against gnies 0.3.3, the authors' package
build: Andrey pre-release build of 3 November 2026 (version string 0.13.0) for every fit but the order check, which ran on a build of the same day that adds DEBUG records of the steps a tie decided; with the records off, its GIES and GES outputs equal the first build's

regimes.gnies_a: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational + 3 environments, mean degree 2.7, 1 target per environment, v ~ U[5, 10]; in claim, figure (Fig. 3)
regimes.gnies_b: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational + 3 environments, mean degree 4, 1 target per environment, v ~ U[5, 10]; in claim, figure (Fig. 8)
regimes.gnies_c: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational + 3 environments, mean degree 2.7, 3 targets per environment, v ~ U[5, 10]; in claim, figure (Fig. 9)
regimes.gnies_d: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational + 3 environments, mean degree 2.7, 1 target per environment, v ~ U[3, 4]; in claim, text (Sec. 5.1)
regimes.gnies_e: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, 4 environments, none observational, mean degree 2.7, 1 target each, v ~ U[5, 10]; in claim, claim (Sec. 5.1)
regimes.gnies_f: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational + 9 environments, mean degree 2.7, 1 target each, v ~ U[5, 10]; in claim, claim (Sec. 1 and 6)
regimes.gnies_g: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational 1,000 rows + 3 environments of 100, 1 target each, v ~ U[5, 10]; in claim, claim
regimes.gnies_h1: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational + 1 environment, 1 target, v ~ U[5, 10]; in claim, claim (Theorem 1)
regimes.gnies_h2: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational + 2 environments, 1 target each, v ~ U[5, 10]; in claim, claim (Theorem 1)
regimes.gnies_s: linear-Gaussian data from 10-variable Erdos-Renyi graphs, observational + 3 environments, signed weights, unit noise variance, 1 target each, noise variance multiplied by U[5, 10] / U[1, 2]; in claim, claim
regimes.gnies_hard: the A design with hard interventions: the target's mechanism replaced by N(0, v), v ~ U[5, 10]; out of claim
regimes.gnies_mean_shift: the A design with a mean shift of 2 observational standard deviations at each target, noise variances unchanged; out of claim
regimes.gnies_weights_halved: the A design with each target's incoming weights halved, noise unchanged; out of claim
regimes.gnies_laplace: the A design with Laplace noise, noise variance multiplied by U[5, 10] / U[1, 2]; out of claim
regimes.gnies_nonlinear: the A design with additive nonlinear equations and unit noise, noise variance multiplied by U[5, 10] / U[1, 2]; out of claim
regimes.gnies_variables: the A design with 1,000 rows per environment at 20, 30, 50, and 100 variables, seeds 0-9; the reference ran 10 seeds at 20 variables and 3 at 30, under a 3,600 s cap per fit; out of claim

verdict_rule: per cell and per metric (shd, target_error), D = error(Andrey at its defaults) - error(gnies at its defaults) per dataset, on datasets both finished and the model check passed; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs is reported, not judged. 10,000 resamples of the datasets, the generator seeded by the CRC-32 of '<cell>/<metric>/<comparison>'. A worse cell counts only if its rerun on seeds 20-39 is worse too; a better cell is cited only if its rerun is better too. Floors: in every cell with 100 or more rows per environment, the interval of shd(Andrey) - shd(empty) and of target_error(Andrey) - |true targets| must lie entirely below 0; in a cell with 10 rows per environment the shd floor applies only when the reference's own interval against the empty graph lies entirely below 0, and the target-error floor does not apply. Out-of-claim cells are reported and never judged
fit_protocol: every arm of a dataset back to back on one pinned core with one BLAS thread; a cap of 1,800 s per fit at 10 variables (300 s for gnies with the true targets fixed) and 3,600 s on the variable ladder; a fit past its cap is a timeout, never an empty graph; a gnies fit whose total is not finite or whose local scores returned NaN is an error and leaves its cell's pairs
error_metric: each entry's own, in its error_metric and metric: the SHD of the interventional essential graph or the target error, as the median over the paired datasets (the _mean fields hold the means)

hardware.note: cpu_models is the CPU of the gate, rerun, out-of-claim, and ladder fits, on 24 hosts; the order check, which counts results and not times, ran on one more host, whose CPU model was not recorded

complete_definition: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a setting with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted in the timeout columns and never scored
seeds_note: seeds is the number of datasets attempted per setting: 20 (seeds 0-19) in every in-claim and out-of-claim setting at 10 variables, with reruns on seeds 20-39 in the replication of the 7 settings that came out better; 10 (seeds 0-9) on the ladder of 20 to 100 variables, where the reference ran 10 seeds at 20 variables, 3 at 30, and none at 50 and 100

methods.comparator_setting: every default: the standard BIC (lmbda = 0.5 * log(N)), the greedy outer search with its forward and backward phases, and the inner search with forward, backward, and turning phases, repeated while the score improves
methods.hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread
methods.same_graph_test: equal marks of the interventional essential graph (same_graph) and equal targets (same_targets)
methods.error_metric: SHD of the returned interventional essential graph against the true one, the true DAG with every edge at a true target oriented: one per variable pair whose edge differs (missing, extra, or oriented differently). andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means
